This work does not suit people who move slowly, dislike constant social contact, or cannot tolerate smoke and alcohol exposure. Players celebrate wins and vent after losses, while dealers must keep a professional expression throughout the shift.

A common path is casino or dealer-school training, proficiency in games such as 21 (blackjack), roulette, or sic bo, qualification for live tables, and advancement into pit supervision or other casino operations roles.

This work suits people with quick hands, strong mental arithmetic, confidence, and stamina for night shifts. Dealers distribute cards, announce results, and track bets at the same time. That coordinated pace is not easy to sustain.

Gambling Dealers run games in legal casinos. They shuffle and deal cards, announce results, calculate payouts, collect and pay chips, and maintain table order. They also watch for irregular activity and follow casino compliance procedures, making them central to front-line casino operations.
